entry.title: A part in washing hands
entry.summary: Davies includes handwashing among the care routines toddlers can join, with help as their skills grow. The child does not have to manage every part.
entry.cue: Your child may want a turn with the soap, the towel, or a movement they have watched you make.
detail: Her sink example keeps soap and a towel with the routine. She pairs handwashing with other gradually shared care, such as hair brushing and nose wiping.

The book also describes a separate handwashing table for a child who wants to repeat washing at the sink and can carry a jug. That is a different setup, not something every family needs to create. Ordinary washing together can offer a part to join.
